packageText: TITLE: Testicular Carcinoma Staging SOURCE STATUS - [Both] This fused master source combines RadPrimer Testicular Carcinoma with STATdx Testicular Carcinoma Staging. - [RadPrimer] Canonical hierarchy: All Categories > Basic > Ultrasound > Scrotum Basic > Testicular Carcinoma - [RadPrimer] Canonical deck path: Corebook::Ultrasound::Scrotum Basic::Testicular Carcinoma::Testicular Carcinoma Staging - [Both] Core Radiology evidence was requested but not supplied in this browser bundle; do not label later output as Core-supported unless a later run provides auditable Core text. MASTER SUMMARY - [Both] Testicular carcinoma is usually a malignant germ cell tumor presenting as a discrete intratesticular mass; ultrasound is the primary diagnostic test, while CT abdomen/pelvis, chest imaging, selected MR, and selected PET/bone/brain imaging support staging and restaging. - [RadPrimer] The key imaging clue is a hypoechoic or mixed echogenic testicular mass, often with abnormal vascularity. A discrete grayscale mass with intrinsic vessels should be treated as suspicious for malignancy. - [STATdx] AJCC staging applies to postpubertal germ cell tumors and malignant sex cord-stromal tumors; it does not apply to spermatocytic tumor, nonmalignant sex cord-stromal tumor, prepubertal germ cell tumor, hematolymphoid tumor, or paratesticular neoplasm. - [Both] Germ cell tumors account for most malignant testicular tumors. Seminoma is commonly homogeneous, hypoechoic, solid, and vascular; nonseminomatous tumors are more likely heterogeneous, ill-defined, cystic, calcified, hemorrhagic, necrotic, or invasive. PRIMARY TUMOR DETECTION AND LOCAL CHARACTERIZATION - [RadPrimer] Ultrasound identifies and characterizes the scrotal mass. Use a high-frequency linear transducer. Most tumors are unilateral; contralateral tumor can occur, usually asynchronously. - [STATdx] Ultrasound is nearly 100% sensitive for detecting scrotal masses and usually distinguishes intratesticular from extratesticular masses, but it cannot reliably subtype most tumors; orchiectomy provides definitive staging and histology. - [Both] Seminoma tends to be well-defined, hypoechoic, solid, and relatively homogeneous; larger seminomas may be heterogeneous or lobulated. Doppler commonly shows increased vascularity compared with normal testis. - [Both] Teratoma and mixed nonseminomatous tumors often show complex cystic/solid architecture, calcification, cartilage/bone elements, fibrosis, hemorrhage, or necrosis. - [Both] Embryonal carcinoma is often heterogeneous, poorly marginated, predominantly solid, and may invade the tunica albuginea or distort the testicular contour. - [Both] Choriocarcinoma can be small and echogenic but is notable for hemorrhage/necrosis/calcification and early hematogenous metastasis, especially to lung and brain. - [STATdx] MR is not routine for initial evaluation, but can help in complicated cases and can demonstrate tunica albuginea/vaginalis, spermatic cord, and scrotal invasion. Seminoma on MR is often sharply defined, multinodular, T2 hypointense, and may show enhancing fibrovascular septa; NSGCT is more heterogeneous and ill-defined. STAGING FRAMEWORK - [STATdx] Imaging is not the standard method for pathologic T staging; radical inguinal orchiectomy with pathologic assessment determines local tumor extent and histologic subtype composition. - [STATdx] T1 disease is limited to testis including rete testis invasion, without lymphovascular invasion; pure seminoma is subdivided by size into pT1a under 3 cm and pT1b at least 3 cm. - [STATdx] T2 disease is limited to testis with lymphovascular invasion, hilar soft tissue/epididymal invasion, or penetration of the visceral mesothelial layer covering the external tunica albuginea. - [STATdx] T3 disease invades the spermatic cord. T4 disease invades the scrotum. - [STATdx] CT abdomen/pelvis is indicated for initial regional nodal staging. Suspicious nodes are low attenuation or poorly enhancing in typical drainage locations; an 8-mm short-axis threshold in typical retroperitoneal locations is specific but insensitive. - [STATdx] N1 means single or multiple regional nodes up to 2 cm short axis; N2 means nodes over 2 cm and up to 5 cm; N3 means nodes over 5 cm. - [STATdx] Nonregional nodal or pulmonary metastases define M1a disease. Nonpulmonary visceral metastases, including liver, brain, bone, kidney, or adrenal disease, define M1b disease. - [STATdx] Serum marker category is part of post-orchiectomy staging: LDH, beta-hCG, and AFP define S0-S3 severity groups. Elevated markers after orchiectomy can make stage IS disease even when imaging is negative. NODAL AND METASTATIC SPREAD - [Both] Testicular germ cell tumors usually spread first by lymphatics to retroperitoneal nodes. Right testicular tumors first involve right-sided nodes around the IVC, commonly aortocaval/paracaval nodes. Left testicular tumors first involve paraaortic/preaortic nodes in the region bounded by the renal vein, aorta, ureter, and inferior mesenteric artery. - [STATdx] Inguinal or pelvic nodes are regional only when lymphatics have been disrupted by prior scrotal/inguinal surgery or tumor-contaminated scrotum; otherwise isolated inguinal nodes should be considered nonregional disease. - [STATdx] Above-diaphragm nodal disease can spread via thoracic duct in seminoma; NSGCT spread is more random and can involve anterior mediastinal, aortopulmonary window, hilar, supraclavicular, and neck nodes. - [Both] Hematogenous spread is late except for choriocarcinoma. Lung is the most common distant site; liver, brain, bone, kidney, and adrenal metastases are also important. - [RadPrimer] CT/MR evaluate nodal and metastatic disease; PET can help evaluate post-treatment residual masses, especially seminoma, but negative PET does not exclude teratoma/NSGCT residual disease. STAGE GROUPS AND RISK - [RadPrimer] Stage I is confined to testis; stage II involves nodes below the diaphragm; stage III involves lymph nodes above the diaphragm or extranodal metastases. - [STATdx] Stage IIA corresponds to limited N1 nodal disease; stage IIB corresponds to N2 disease; stage IIC corresponds to N3 disease. M1a disease includes nonregional nodes or pulmonary metastases. M1b disease includes nonpulmonary visceral metastases and is stage IIIC. - [STATdx] Good-risk disease has no nonpulmonary visceral metastases and favorable marker/site profiles; intermediate and poor risk are driven by nonseminoma mediastinal primary, nonpulmonary visceral metastases, and higher AFP/beta-hCG/LDH categories. DIFFERENTIAL DIAGNOSIS AND PITFALLS - [RadPrimer] Important mimics include epidermoid cyst, lymphoma, subacute hematoma, segmental infarct, and focal orchitis. - [RadPrimer] Consider lymphoma in older patients, bilateral or multifocal lesions, and associated lymphadenopathy elsewhere. - [STATdx] Burned-out germ cell tumor can present as a metastatic retroperitoneal mass with only a tiny scar, cystic focus, or calcified testicular lesion; always image the testes in the appropriate patient with retroperitoneal germ-cell-type disease. - [STATdx] Microlithiasis without mass is controversial as a risk factor; most recommendations favor self-exam rather than routine ultrasound screening when no mass is present. TREATMENT AND FOLLOW-UP ORIENTATION - [Both] Radical inguinal orchiectomy is the diagnostic and initial therapeutic step for most suspected testicular carcinoma. - [RadPrimer] Seminoma is radiosensitive and chemotherapy-sensitive. Nonseminomatous tumors are treated with orchiectomy, chemotherapy, and/or retroperitoneal lymph node dissection depending on stage and response. - [STATdx] Stage and histology drive surveillance, radiation, chemotherapy, and residual-mass management. Seminoma residual masses with normal markers may be evaluated with FDG PET; NSGCT residual masses often require resection because teratoma can be PET-negative. IMAGE CURATION SUMMARY - [Both] Actual image_evidence files were inspected using generated contact sheets. No exact duplicate, same-slice, same-screenshot, or unusable source image was identified. - [Both] All RadPrimer and STATdx images remain in the primary teaching set. STATdx images are not used to archive RadPrimer images; they add staging diagrams, MR/CT examples, nodal stage variants, and metastatic pattern reinforcement. - [Both] Preserve same-patient STATdx clusters when using their images in later narrative/card generation. IMAGE APPENDIX - RadPrimer image 1: Graphic shows a multilobulated testicular mass . Note the compressed and near complete replacement of normal testicular parenchyma . Teaching role: canonicalBackbone, primaryTumorAppearance. - RadPrimer image 2: Longitudinal color Doppler ultrasound shows a solid, homogeneous, hypoechoic testicular mass with increased peripheral vascularity . Features suggest testicular seminoma. Teaching role: canonicalBackbone, primaryTumorAppearance. - RadPrimer image 3: Longitudinal power Doppler ultrasound shows a small, well-defined, hypoechoic vascular testicular mass suggestive of small testicular seminoma. Teaching role: canonicalBackbone, primaryTumorAppearance. - RadPrimer image 4: Longitudinal ultrasound shows a multilocular cystic testicular mass, with cysts of varying echogenicity in a cystic teratoma. Note calcific foci with posterior acoustic shadowing. Teaching role: canonicalBackbone, primaryTumorAppearance. - RadPrimer image 5: Transverse ultrasound shows an isoechoic area of choriocarcinoma invading the tunica albuginea & adjacent hypoechoic mixed germ cell tumor . Teaching role: canonicalBackbone, primaryTumorAppearance. - RadPrimer image 6: Transverse ultrasound of the testis shows a mixed germ cell tumor seen as a large, irregular, heterogeneous mass invading tunica albuginea . Teaching role: canonicalBackbone, primaryTumorAppearance. - RadPrimer image 7: Oblique ultrasound shows an ill-defined, irregular, hypoechoic, heterogeneous mass invading the tunica albuginea . Final diagnosis: Embryonal cell carcinoma. Teaching role: canonicalBackbone, primaryTumorAppearance. - RadPrimer image 8: Transverse CECT shows a conglomerate of metastatic para-aortic and retroperitoneal lymph nodes in patient with testicular cancer. Teaching role: canonicalBackbone, metastaticStaging. - STATdx image 1: Graphic shows T1 disease. The primary tumor is limited to the testis (including rete testis invasion) without lymphovascular invasion. For pure seminoma, pT1 is subdivided into pT1a when the tumor is < 3 cm in size and pT1b when the tumor is ≥ 3 cm in size. Teaching role: tStageGraphic, stagingFramework; cluster: STATdx T-stage graphics. - STATdx image 2: Graphic shows T2 disease. The primary tumor is limited to the testis (including rete testis invasion) with lymphovascular invasion or tumor invading hilar soft tissue or the epididymis or penetrating visceral mesothelial layer covering external surface of the tunica albuginea ± lymphovascular invasion. Teaching role: tStageGraphic, stagingFramework; cluster: STATdx T-stage graphics. - STATdx image 3: Graphic shows T3 disease. The primary tumor invades the spermatic cord ± lymphovascular invasion. Teaching role: tStageGraphic, stagingFramework; cluster: STATdx T-stage graphics. - STATdx image 4: Graphic shows T4 disease. The primary tumor invades the scrotum ± lymphovascular invasion. Teaching role: tStageGraphic, stagingFramework; cluster: STATdx T-stage graphics. - STATdx image 5: Right testicular nodal spread initially involves the aortocaval and paracaval nodes (dotted white line). Inguinal or pelvic nodes are considered regional lymph nodes if there has been disruption of lymphatics from prior scrotal or inguinal surgery . The size of the nodes determines N stage: N1 < 2 cm, N2 2-5 cm, N3 > 5 cm. Teaching role: nodalDrainageGraphic, stagingFramework; cluster: STATdx nodal drainage graphics. - STATdx image 6: Left testicular spread involves a retroperitoneal area bounded by the renal vein, aorta, ureter, and inferior vena cava (dotted white line). Inguinal or pelvic nodes are considered regional lymph nodes if there has been disruption of lymphatics from prior scrotal or inguinal surgery . Teaching role: nodalDrainageGraphic, stagingFramework; cluster: STATdx nodal drainage graphics. - STATdx image 7: Text not available. Teaching role: nodalDrainageGraphic, stagingFramework. - STATdx image 8: Longitudinal US in a 22-year-old man who presented with testicular discomfort shows a small, solid, hypoechoic, homogeneous intratesticular mass . A few scattered microcalcifications are present within the testis. Teaching role: primaryTumorAppearance, modalityVariant, recognitionReinforcement; cluster: STATdx small seminoma US/MR same-patient cluster. - STATdx image 9: Color Doppler US in the same patient shows increased vascularity in the testicular mass . There is no elevation of tumor markers. Teaching role: primaryTumorAppearance, modalityVariant, recognitionReinforcement; cluster: STATdx small seminoma US/MR same-patient cluster. - STATdx image 10: Axial T2 MR in the same patient shows a 7-mm left testicular mass , well seen against the high signal of normal parenchyma. Linear low signal represents the mediastinum testis. Teaching role: primaryTumorAppearance, modalityVariant, recognitionReinforcement; cluster: STATdx small seminoma US/MR same-patient cluster. - STATdx image 11: Axial T1 C+ FS MR in the same patient shows an enhancing, 7-mm left testicular mass . Pathologic examination following orchiectomy revealed a 7-mm seminoma. For a pure seminoma, tumor < 3 cm in size is staged as pT1a. Teaching role: primaryTumorAppearance, modalityVariant, recognitionReinforcement; cluster: STATdx small seminoma US/MR same-patient cluster. - STATdx image 12: Coronal T2 MR shows a circumscribed, homogeneous, hypointense mass in the left testicle . Although imaging is not used for T staging of testicular tumors, MR is the best imaging modality to evaluate for tunica and spermatic cord involvement, neither of which were involved in this case. Pathology revealed seminoma. Teaching role: primaryTumorAppearance, modalityVariant, recognitionReinforcement; cluster: STATdx MR seminoma same-patient cluster. - STATdx image 13: Axial T1 C+ MR in the same patient shows homogeneous enhancement in the left testicular mass with sparing of the low-signal tunica . Teaching role: primaryTumorAppearance, modalityVariant, recognitionReinforcement; cluster: STATdx MR seminoma same-patient cluster. - STATdx image 14: Grayscale US in a 44-year-old man who presented with testicular swelling shows a solid, hypoechoic, heterogeneous intratesticular mass . Teaching role: primaryTumorAppearance, modalityVariant, recognitionReinforcement; cluster: STATdx heterogeneous seminoma US same-patient cluster. - STATdx image 15: Color Doppler US in the same patient shows increased vascularity of the testicular mass . There is no elevation of tumor markers. Pathologic examination following orchiectomy revealed a mixed germ cell tumor limited to the testis with involvement of the hilar structures. Teaching role: primaryTumorAppearance, modalityVariant, recognitionReinforcement; cluster: STATdx heterogeneous seminoma US same-patient cluster. - STATdx image 16: Axial T2 MR shows a heterogeneous, hypointense mass replacing the majority of normal testicular tissue of the left side of the undescended testicle. The tunica vaginalis has been invaded . Teaching role: primaryTumorAppearance, modalityVariant, recognitionReinforcement; cluster: STATdx undescended-testis tumor MR cluster. - STATdx image 17: Sagittal T2 MR in the same patient shows a large, hypointense mass replacing the majority of normal testicular tissue in the undescended testicle. Disruption of the tunica vaginalis is again shown . Teaching role: primaryTumorAppearance, modalityVariant, recognitionReinforcement; cluster: STATdx undescended-testis tumor MR cluster. - STATdx image 18: Axial T2 MR shows a large, heterogeneous, predominantly isointense mass replacing the majority of the normal right testicle. The tunica vaginalis is invaded . Teaching role: primaryTumorAppearance, modalityVariant, recognitionReinforcement; cluster: STATdx tunica invasion pathology cluster. - STATdx image 19: Gross pathology from the same patient correlates to imaging findings with the mass replacing the majority of testicular tissue as well as invasion through the tunica vaginalis . Teaching role: primaryTumorAppearance, modalityVariant, recognitionReinforcement; cluster: STATdx tunica invasion pathology cluster. - STATdx image 20: Grayscale US in a 46-year-old man who presented with testicular swelling shows a solid, hypoechoic, heterogeneous left intratesticular mass with small foci of calcifications . Teaching role: primaryTumorAppearance, modalityVariant, recognitionReinforcement; cluster: STATdx N1 stage IIA cluster. - STATdx image 21: Axial CECT in the same patient shows a 1.8-cm left paraaortic lymph node . Testicular masses, regardless of pT staging, with < 5 nodes measuring < 2 cm each (N1), are designated stage IIA. Teaching role: nodalStaging, stageVariant, recognitionReinforcement; cluster: STATdx N1 stage IIA cluster. - STATdx image 22: Color Doppler US in a 34-year-old man shows an enlarged, hypoechoic left testis with increased vascularity. There is no elevation of tumor markers. Pathologic examination following orchiectomy revealed mixed germ cell tumor involving the hilum. Teaching role: nodalStaging, stageVariant, recognitionReinforcement; cluster: STATdx N2 stage IIB cluster. - STATdx image 23: Axial CECT in the same patient shows a 3.5-cm left paraaortic lymph node . Testicular masses, regardless of pT staging, with < 5 nodes measuring > 2 cm but < 5 cm (N2), are designated stage IIB. Teaching role: nodalStaging, stageVariant, recognitionReinforcement; cluster: STATdx N2 stage IIB cluster. - STATdx image 24: Axial CECT in a 30-year-old man shows a 7.2-cm left paraaortic necrotic mass . Teaching role: nodalStaging, stageVariant, recognitionReinforcement; cluster: STATdx N3/burned-out tumor cluster. - STATdx image 25: Grayscale US in the same patient shows a small, hypoechoic intratesticular mass with a small area of calcification . Varicocele is noted posterior to the mass. This case represents an example of a burned-out germ cell tumor where the primary testicular germ cell tumor may be small or involute in the setting of widespread metastatic disease and appears as a small mass with a cystic area ± focal calcification. Teaching role: nodalStaging, stageVariant, recognitionReinforcement; cluster: STATdx N3/burned-out tumor cluster. - STATdx image 26: US in a 28-year-old man who presented with scrotal swelling shows an enlarged, heterogeneous left testis and left hydrocele . Compare the echogenicity of the left testis to that of the normal right testis . Teaching role: localExtension, caseCluster, recognitionReinforcement; cluster: STATdx spermatic-cord/local-extension cluster. - STATdx image 27: US in the same patient shows an enlarged, heterogeneous left testis and complex left hydrocele with low-level echoes, likely due to hemorrhage. Teaching role: localExtension, caseCluster, recognitionReinforcement; cluster: STATdx spermatic-cord/local-extension cluster. - STATdx image 28: Left inguinal color Doppler US in the same patient shows an enlarged, heterogeneous, minimally vascularized left spermatic cord . Teaching role: localExtension, caseCluster, recognitionReinforcement; cluster: STATdx spermatic-cord/local-extension cluster. - STATdx image 29: Axial CECT in the same patient shows an enlarged left spermatic cord . Although imaging is usually not adequate for T staging of testicular tumors, in this case, the presence of spermatic cord enlargement continuous with the testicular mass is highly suggestive of T3 tumor, which was confirmed on pathologic examination following orchiectomy. Teaching role: localExtension, caseCluster, recognitionReinforcement; cluster: STATdx spermatic-cord/local-extension cluster. - STATdx image 30: Axial CECT in the same patient shows a large, mixed solid and cystic left testicular mass . Teaching role: localExtension, caseCluster, recognitionReinforcement; cluster: STATdx spermatic-cord/local-extension cluster. - STATdx image 31: Coronal CECT in the same patient shows a left testicular mass , an enlarged left spermatic cord , and a large retroperitoneal nodal mass with a mixed solid and cystic appearance, similar to the primary testicular mass. AFP level was 2,355 ng/mL, consistent with S2. Teaching role: localExtension, caseCluster, recognitionReinforcement; cluster: STATdx spermatic-cord/local-extension cluster. - STATdx image 32: Color Doppler US of the right testis in a 21-year-old man who presented with testicular discomfort shows a heavily calcified mass with posterior shadowing. There is a small hydrocele . Teaching role: advancedNodalMetastasis, caseCluster, recognitionReinforcement; cluster: STATdx bulky nodal and M1a cluster. - STATdx image 33: Longitudinal US in the same patient shows a separate solid, hypoechoic intratesticular mass . Teaching role: advancedNodalMetastasis, caseCluster, recognitionReinforcement; cluster: STATdx bulky nodal and M1a cluster. - STATdx image 34: Axial CECT in the same patient shows a 9-cm retroperitoneal aortocaval nodal mass that appears to encase the inferior vena cava and abut the aorta . Teaching role: advancedNodalMetastasis, caseCluster, recognitionReinforcement; cluster: STATdx bulky nodal and M1a cluster. - STATdx image 35: Coronal CECT in the same patient shows the retroperitoneal mass actually invading the inferior vena cava . Biopsy revealed a yolk sac tumor. AFP level was 6,411 ng/mL, consistent with S2. Orchiectomy revealed pT2 disease. Teaching role: advancedNodalMetastasis, caseCluster, recognitionReinforcement; cluster: STATdx bulky nodal and M1a cluster. - STATdx image 36: Axial CECT in the same patient shows an enlarged left supraclavicular lymph node . Teaching role: advancedNodalMetastasis, caseCluster, recognitionReinforcement; cluster: STATdx bulky nodal and M1a cluster. - STATdx image 37: Coronal CECT in the same patient shows an enlarged left supraclavicular lymph node as well as a pulmonary metastatic lesion . Nonretroperitoneal nodal or pulmonary metastases constitute M1a disease. Teaching role: advancedNodalMetastasis, caseCluster, recognitionReinforcement; cluster: STATdx bulky nodal and M1a cluster. - STATdx image 38: Sagittal T1 C+ MR shows mild, irregular, heterogeneous enhancement throughout an enlarged left testicle. No focal mass lesion is identified. Note the normal appearance of the left spermatic cord . Teaching role: m1bMetastaticDisease, caseCluster, modalityVariant; cluster: STATdx teratomatous M1b cluster. - STATdx image 39: Axial T1 C+ MR in the same patient shows an enlarged, heterogeneous, poorly enhancing left testicle compared to a normal right testicle . Teaching role: m1bMetastaticDisease, caseCluster, modalityVariant; cluster: STATdx teratomatous M1b cluster. - STATdx image 40: Axial T1 in-phase MR in the same patient shows a heterogeneous retroperitoneal mass . The left psoas muscle is invaded . Teaching role: m1bMetastaticDisease, caseCluster, modalityVariant; cluster: STATdx teratomatous M1b cluster. - STATdx image 41: Axial T1 opposed-phase MR in the same patient shows a heterogeneous retroperitoneal mass. Signal drop on opposed-phase compared to in-phase sequence corresponds to fat elements in the mass, indicating the presence of a teratomatous element. Teaching role: m1bMetastaticDisease, caseCluster, modalityVariant; cluster: STATdx teratomatous M1b cluster. - STATdx image 42: Axial CECT in the same patient shows a large, heterogeneous retroperitoneal mass displacing the aorta and invading the left psoas muscle . A lytic lesion is seen in the L3 vertebral body . Teaching role: m1bMetastaticDisease, caseCluster, modalityVariant; cluster: STATdx teratomatous M1b cluster. - STATdx image 43: Coronal bone scan in the same patient shows uptake in the L3 vertebral lytic lesion , consistent with metastatic disease. Nonpulmonary visceral metastases are consistent with M1b (stage IIIC) disease. Teaching role: m1bMetastaticDisease, caseCluster, modalityVariant; cluster: STATdx teratomatous M1b cluster. - STATdx image 44: Longitudinal US shows a heterogeneous intratesticular mass with foci of calcifications in the setting of microlithiasis . Pathology revealed teratoma isolated to the testicle without tunica or spermatic cord invasion. Teaching role: m1Disease, caseCluster, modalityVariant; cluster: STATdx widespread metastatic cluster. - STATdx image 45: Axial CECT in the same patient shows a large, heterogeneous, cystic and solid left paraaortic mass with calcified foci . Teaching role: m1Disease, caseCluster, modalityVariant; cluster: STATdx widespread metastatic cluster. - STATdx image 46: Chest x-ray in the same patient shows multiple pulmonary metastatic lesions. Teaching role: m1Disease, caseCluster, modalityVariant; cluster: STATdx widespread metastatic cluster. - STATdx image 47: Axial NECT in the same patient further characterizes multiple pulmonary metastatic lesions, some of which show central cavitation . Teaching role: m1Disease, caseCluster, modalityVariant; cluster: STATdx widespread metastatic cluster. - STATdx image 48: Axial FLAIR MR in the same patient shows an intraaxial metastatic lesion in the right posterior parietal lobe with surrounding vasogenic edema . Teaching role: m1Disease, caseCluster, modalityVariant; cluster: STATdx widespread metastatic cluster. - STATdx image 49: Coronal T1 C+ MR in the same patient shows an intraaxial metastatic lesion in the right parietal lobe with peripheral enhancement . Teaching role: m1Disease, caseCluster, modalityVariant; cluster: STATdx widespread metastatic cluster. GENERATOR NOTES - Use RadPrimer hierarchy/deck routing exactly as supplied in metadata.json. - Use source labels in later prose when a detail is source-specific. - Avoid claiming Core support unless later evidence supplies Core text.

RadPrimer.role: Canonical hierarchy and base testicular carcinoma article.
limitations: Less granular AJCC/TNM staging and fewer metastatic case examples than STATdx.
STATdx breadcrumb is not used for deck hierarchy because RadPrimer is present.

sourceAttributionRules.default: Tag factual blocks as [RadPrimer], [STATdx], or [Both] where the distinction matters.
sourceAttributionRules.humanFacingImages: Use labels like RadPrimer image 5 or STATdx image 24 in prose.
sourceAttributionRules.traceability: Use masterImageId values only in registry/import/report metadata.

textBackbone.primary: RadPrimer supplies the canonical disease article backbone, sonographic appearance by histology, baseline differential, and original hierarchy.
textBackbone.supplement: STATdx supplies the staging-focused TNM/AJCC framework, nodal drainage maps, metastatic work-up, risk/prognostic staging, restaging/surveillance detail, and richer multimodality examples.
textBackbone.downweight: Do not treat either source as Core Radiology. No Core evidence was supplied in this bundle.

sourceSelectionPlan.imageCurationPolicy: Exact duplicates may be archived. Near duplicates, alternate patients, alternate modality examples, stage variants, and conceptual replacements remain in the primaryTeachingSet as recognition reinforcement unless visually identical or unusable.
sourceSelectionPlan.duplicateEvidencePolicy: Exact duplicate calls require visual evidence from image_evidence files, matching source image IDs, image hashes, or explicit source/manual confirmation. Caption-only or topic-only similarity is insufficient.

RP-01: RadPrimer graphic teaches mass replacement; STATdx T-stage graphics teach invasion extent rather than the same graphic.
RP-02: Same seminoma/solid hypoechoic vascular mass teaching need, but different ultrasound images/patients.
RP-03: Small hypoechoic vascular testicular mass concept is covered, but not by the same image.
RP-04: Cystic/calcified nonseminomatous tumor and burned-out/microlithiasis examples overlap conceptually, but images are visually distinct.
RP-05: Tunica/extratesticular invasion and mixed tumor concept overlaps, but the visual examples are different.
RP-06: Large heterogeneous mass teaching is reinforced by STATdx, but no same image/slice is present.
RP-07: Ill-defined heterogeneous invasive tumor concept is reinforced, but source images are different.
RP-08: Retroperitoneal nodal metastasis is extensively covered by STATdx; CT slices/cases are distinct.

caseClusterGuardrails.policy: Same-patient and stage-demonstration clusters should stay atomic when used in narrative/card generation.
clustersToPreserve: STATdx bulky nodal and M1a cluster
STATdx heterogeneous seminoma US same-patient cluster
STATdx small seminoma US/MR same-patient cluster

generatorInstructions: Use source-qualified human-facing labels such as RadPrimer image 5 and STATdx image 24.
Keep short IDs such as RP-05 and SDX-24 in traceability fields, filenames, and registry metadata.
For cards, separate primary tumor recognition, TNM staging, nodal pathways, serum markers, and metastatic-risk groups rather than mixing them into overloaded prompts.
Do not generate unsupported Core cross-check statements from this master source.

textBackbone.primary: RadPrimer supplies the canonical disease article backbone, sonographic appearance by histology, baseline differential, and original hierarchy.
textBackbone.supplement: STATdx supplies the staging-focused TNM/AJCC framework, nodal drainage maps, metastatic work-up, risk/prognostic staging, restaging/surveillance detail, and richer multimodality examples.
textBackbone.downweight: Do not treat either source as Core Radiology. No Core evidence was supplied in this bundle.

sourceSelectionPlan.imageCurationPolicy: Exact duplicates may be archived. Near duplicates, alternate patients, alternate modality examples, stage variants, and conceptual replacements remain in the primaryTeachingSet as recognition reinforcement unless visually identical or unusable.
sourceSelectionPlan.duplicateEvidencePolicy: Exact duplicate calls require visual evidence from image_evidence files, matching source image IDs, image hashes, or explicit source/manual confirmation. Caption-only or topic-only similarity is insufficient.

RP-01: RadPrimer graphic teaches mass replacement; STATdx T-stage graphics teach invasion extent rather than the same graphic.
RP-02: Same seminoma/solid hypoechoic vascular mass teaching need, but different ultrasound images/patients.
RP-03: Small hypoechoic vascular testicular mass concept is covered, but not by the same image.
RP-04: Cystic/calcified nonseminomatous tumor and burned-out/microlithiasis examples overlap conceptually, but images are visually distinct.
RP-05: Tunica/extratesticular invasion and mixed tumor concept overlaps, but the visual examples are different.
RP-06: Large heterogeneous mass teaching is reinforced by STATdx, but no same image/slice is present.
RP-07: Ill-defined heterogeneous invasive tumor concept is reinforced, but source images are different.
RP-08: Retroperitoneal nodal metastasis is extensively covered by STATdx; CT slices/cases are distinct.

caseClusterGuardrails.policy: Same-patient and stage-demonstration clusters should stay atomic when used in narrative/card generation.

generatorInstructions: Use source-qualified human-facing labels such as RadPrimer image 5 and STATdx image 24.
Keep short IDs such as RP-05 and SDX-24 in traceability fields, filenames, and registry metadata.
For cards, separate primary tumor recognition, TNM staging, nodal pathways, serum markers, and metastatic-risk groups rather than mixing them into overloaded prompts.
Do not generate unsupported Core cross-check statements from this master source.
